provenance.source_type: python (stored Aspen cracker activities + literature-calibrated turbine inputs)
provenance.inputs_summary: stored Aspen baseline cracker; Ahmad 2025 turbine end points; reference scenario costs; literature ranges from research/data

what_each_pathway_assumes.direct: Ahmad Case 2a system efficiency 49.12 % on LHV 18.8 = 9.2346 MJ electricity per kg NH3 = 49.64 % on the AmCraX LHV 18.60 MJ/kg.
what_each_pathway_assumes.full_fired / partial_fired: Cracker heat = stored Aspen reactor + pre-heater duty (3.291 MJ per kg NH3 cracked) supplied by burning extra NH3 at 100 % heat-transfer efficiency (assumption, favourable to cracking). Combined cycle on the H2/N2(/NH3) fuel gas LHV at eta_h2_fuel = 49.64 % (copy of the direct value; assumption eta_gt_gas).
what_each_pathway_assumes.full_purified / blend_purified: Stored Aspen baseline cracker + PSA (recovery 0.85); heat deficit after tail-gas firing from extra NH3; combined cycle on the H2 (or NH3 + H2 blend) LHV at eta_h2_fuel = 49.64 % (assumption).
what_each_pathway_assumes.full_exhaust / partial_exhaust: Electricity per kg NH3 from Ahmad's two system end points (49.12 % and about 54 % on LHV 18.8, i.e. 49.64 % and 54.58 % on LHV 18.60, +4.93 pp), linear in the cracked share (assumption). No extra NH3 for cracker heat (exhaust supplies it) and ETA_GT_GAS is NOT used. The implied combined-cycle efficiency on cracked-gas LHV is 47.78 % (below 49.64 %, because exhaust heat goes to the cracker instead of the steam cycle).
what_each_pathway_assumes.double_counting_check: Ahmad's efficiency gain enters only the exhaust-heated kinds through eta_exhaust_integrated(); those kinds neither add cracker-heat NH3 nor apply ETA_GT_GAS, and the fired/purified kinds never use the Ahmad 54 % value. Nothing is counted twice (validation EU-P2-no-double-count).
what_each_pathway_assumes.brief_correction: The statement that all four stored power costs assume a 49.64 % hydrogen-rich turbine is true for fired cracking (280.1) and cracking + PSA (310.2) only. The exhaust-heated value (255.6) uses Ahmad's 54 % system efficiency.

statement_of_result.text: On the unified reference scenario (grey NH3 450 USD/t, 8000 h/yr, 10 %, 25 y), direct NH3 combustion gives 258.9 USD/MWh. It is 7.6 % cheaper than a standalone fired cracker (280.1) and 16.5 % cheaper than cracking + PSA (310.2), as 1 - direct/cracking, ON THE ASSUMPTION that the turbine reaches the direct-NH3 efficiency (49.64 %) on the H2-rich fuel. Against an exhaust-heated cracker (Ahmad's +4.93 pp system gain) direct use is 1.3 % dearer (255.6).

old_pre_unification.source: Phase 1 end-use results of the 23 November 2026 release (LCOE 259 / 273 / 304 / 248 USD/MWh), quoted as about 5 to 15 %

exhaust_heated_system_delta_pp.basis: combined-cycle system efficiency on NH3 LHV supplied, exhaust-heated cracker; Ahmad 4.4-5.4 pp on LHV 18.8 rescaled by 18.8/18.6; Karpilov unit and basis not stated ('up to', a maximum over TIT 800-1200 C)
exhaust_heated_system_delta_pp.grade: cycle_simulation (no measurement); small or idealised machines only; nothing for F/H class

fired_H2N2_fuel_delta_pp.basis: nothing sourced for a turbine on H2/N2 from a standalone fired cracker. Bracket for orientation only: lower = Ahmad exhaust-heated implied efficiency on cracked-gas LHV (derived here, exhaust heat diverted to the cracker); upper = NETL 2023 vs 2024 pure H2 (steam-diluted) minus NH3, +7.3 pp, which the literature note says NOT to use for cracked gas.

purified_H2_fuel_delta_pp.basis: NETL 2023 (66.9 %, 100 % H2 steam-diluted, Exhibit 4-9) minus NETL 2024 (59.6 %, 100 % NH3, Exhibit 4-6), same agency method and B32A baseline, H-class-like. Steam dilution inflates the H2 figure, so it is an UPPER bound for dry H2 firing. No lower-side source.
purified_H2_fuel_delta_pp.grade: cycle_simulation, not like-for-like (no cracker, steam diluent)

cracker_heat_fuel_efficiency_sensitivity.description: Computed. Reference-basis turbine-efficiency thresholds (grey 450 USD/t, 8000 h, reference cracker CAPEX) with the extra NH3 for cracker heat delivered at 100 % of its LHV (reference, optimistic), at the stored flowsheet's tail-gas ratio and at the 0.85 H3 furnace efficiency. Direct NH3 is unaffected (no cracker heat). The reference outputs above are at 1.0 and are not changed.

forty_percent_figure.claim: direct NH3 combustion about 40 % cheaper than cracking-based power (essay, attributed to Halim et al. 2025)
forty_percent_figure.halim_status: Full text not accessible (A*STAR repository: request a copy; abstract read; DOI resolves). The abstract supports only the direction (direct use preferable because cracking has high capital and operating cost). 40 %, 60.1 MW, LCOH 15.1 / 10.1 USD/kg and the 30-60 vol% H-25 range are not in the abstract and could not be located. No location can be given for any of them.

sg_low_carbon_willingness_to_pay.source: S&P Global, 'Power generation firms face high hydrogen costs in Singapore', 7 May 2025: willingness to pay for low-carbon hydrogen in Singapore about 3 USD/kg (search-result summary; article not fetched)

ne_asia_smr_production_cost.source: Argus Hydrogen and Future Fuels, issue 26-01 (6 Jan 2026) sample report, p. 2 'Regional hydrogen cost markers 6 Jan': Northeast Asia baseline SMR, incl. capex 3.06 USD/kg (excl. capex 2.09); read from the PDF text of the cited URL

blue_delivered_east_asia.source: ACE report estimate for delivered cost to East Asia: 5-7 USD/kg blue, 9-11 USD/kg green (search-result summary); 6.0 = midpoint (derived)

low_carbon_offer_fob_malaysia.source: S&P Global, indicative offers of low-carbon hydrogen at about 10 USD/kg FOB Malaysia, May 2025 (search-result summary)

evidence_beyond_definition: Cost against alternatives: grey-NH3 cracked H2 4.015 USD/kg (5.174 SGD/kg) is ABOVE the NE Asia SMR cost marker 3.06 (Argus, read from PDF) and the Singapore willingness to pay about 3.0 (S&P, search summary); break-even NH3 320 and 312 USD/t.

Green NH3 2030 (709 USD/t) gives 5.92 USD/kg, below the blue delivered East Asia midpoint 6.0 (ACE, search summary) and the 10 USD/kg low-carbon offer FOB Malaysia (S&P, search summary); green today (1000) gives 8.06, above 6.0 and below 10.
Carbon intensity: green-NH3 H2 2.4 kg CO2e/kg against SMR 10-12; blue 8.9; grey 19.5 (lca workstream).
Energy: cracker + PSA keeps 87.7 % of NH3 LHV as H2 (stored Aspen). Not like-for-like with an electrical efficiency.
what_does_not_exist: No Singapore hydrogen transaction price; three of four benchmarks are search-summary grade and differ in basis (production cost, willingness to pay, delivered, FOB).
No AmCraX comparison with other H2 import carriers (liquid H2, LOHC) or with local electrolysis.
No end-user (refinery, fuel-cell) cost or value of H2 purity in Singapore; Grade D cost is a lower bound (purification workstream).

The 'loss is larger when H2 is an intermediate fuel' half: with the NETL +7.3 pp upper bound applied absolutely, the cracked + PSA route gives slightly MORE electricity per kg NH3 than direct; applied as a ratio it gives less. The energy ranking is not established independently of the turbine assumption.

H1-a.assumptions: eta_h2_fuel = 49.64 % (copy of direct) for fired and purified; fired cracker heat from NH3 at 100 % transfer efficiency; Cho-itemised cracker capex extrapolated about 30-fold; Ahmad plant capital scaled ^0.67; 8000 h (not sourced).
H1-a.uncertainty: fired threshold over bases 3.29 to 8.79 pp; purified 9.68 to 18.10 pp
H1-a.envelope: AmCraX boundary, grey 450 USD/t (300-1000 checked), 5000-8000 h, capex x0.5-x2 and Ahmad correlation.

threshold.fired_vs_sources: nothing sourced for a standalone fired cracker's turbine: threshold is the finding; indirect bracket: sourced values STRADDLE the threshold
threshold.purified_vs_sources: all sourced values BELOW threshold: direct NH3 cheaper (NETL absolute); all sourced values BELOW threshold: direct NH3 cheaper (NETL ratio); all bases: all sourced values BELOW threshold: direct NH3 cheaper

H1-a.reason: The purified sub-pathway passes the threshold test (the only sourced H2-turbine gain, an upper bound, lies below the threshold on every basis checked), but the fired sub-pathway has no sourced turbine efficiency and its threshold lies inside the indirect bracket. The row claims both, so it stays INCONCLUSIVE; the purified half alone would be SUPPORTED inside the stated envelope.

H1-b.uncertainty: Halim's inputs unknown (full text not accessible)
H1-b.envelope: AmCraX boundaries; does not show Halim's own calculation is wrong
H1-b.threshold: existing rule: CONTRADICTED if the largest computed gap is below half the claim (20 %)
H1-b.reason: Largest computed gap is below 20 % on every stored basis; reaching 40 % needs a cracker capital several times the reference (see numbers). The figure could not be located in any accessible Halim text.

H1-c.uncertainty: full-exhaust threshold over bases 1.97 to 8.04 pp
H1-c.envelope: small or mid-size machines (Ahmad 43 MW class, PR 8); no F/H-class source

H1-c.reason: The row says cracking in front of a turbine does not pay. The full-exhaust threshold lies below the like-for-like sourced gains on the reference basis, so on the reference basis the sourced values favour CRACKING (against the row and the essay), but by about 1 % of LCOE, the threshold moves across the supported range when the cracker capex basis or NH3 price changes, and the sensitivity range (0 to 5.5 pp) straddles it. Neither side is clear: INCONCLUSIVE, with the threshold as the finding. Fired partial cracking is dearer than direct at the copy efficiency, but that again follows from the assumption (see partial_fired thresholds).

H1-d.assumptions: stored Aspen PSA split; reference capex; benchmarks of mixed basis and grade
H1-d.uncertainty: benchmarks 3.0-10 USD/kg straddle the computed LCOH range 4.0-8.1
H1-d.envelope: Jurong Island cracker, plant-gate 19.5 bar H2
H1-d.reason: Beyond the definition (H2 is the product, so some conversion is unavoidable) the evidence is a cost comparison against benchmarks that straddle the computed LCOH: cracked grey-NH3 H2 is dearer than NE Asia SMR H2 and the Singapore willingness to pay, cheaper than delivered low-carbon offers. The energy half depends on the turbine assumption (NETL bound applied absolutely reverses it). INCONCLUSIVE.
